# Profiles and tasks

A session setup can be saved in the configuration folder, the folder of
`kapto.toml`, so the same recordings are set up the same way every time:
a **profile** says with which robot, by whom, where and how it is
recorded, and a **task** what the robot is asked to do. The two are
independent: each episode is recorded with a profile and a task chosen
separately, so operators and places change without touching the tasks,
and every profile can record every task. Each is a TOML file known by its name without
`.toml`, which must be an ID: lowercase letters, digits and underscores,
starting with a letter.

Every text must say something: blank values and placeholders such as
`na`, `n/a`, `none`, `-` or `tbd` are refused, since they would be
frozen into every episode recorded with them.

## Profiles: `profiles/<id>.toml`

```toml
# profiles/lab_ana.toml
package = "arm7"
operator = "Ana"
environment = "lab 2, bench A"
mode = "teleoperated"
tags = ["shift-a", "new-gripper"]
notes = "Gripper pads replaced on Monday"
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `package` | yes | The ID of the robot package recorded with it, e.g. `arm7`. |
| `operator` | no | Who operates the robot. |
| `environment` | no | Where it is recorded, e.g. `lab 2, bench A`. |
| `mode` | no | How the robot is driven: `teleoperated` (by a person), `autonomous` (by a policy), `mixed` (a policy a person takes over at times) or `scripted`. |
| `tags` | no | Words to find its episodes by later, e.g. `["shift-a", "new-gripper"]`. |
| `notes` | no | Anything else worth knowing about the recordings, e.g. what changed on the robot. |

## Tasks: `tasks/<id>.toml`

```toml
# tasks/pick_and_place.toml
name = "Pick and place"
description = "Move the cube from the tray to the bin"
prompt = "Pick up the red cube and put it in the bin"
objects = ["red cube", "bin"]
subtasks = ["reach", "grasp", "lift", "place"]
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | no | What people call it, e.g. `Pick and place`. |
| `description` | no | A sentence or two about it. |
| `prompt` | no | The instruction given to the operator or the policy, e.g. `Pick up the red cube and put it in the bin`. |
| `objects` | no | The objects it involves, e.g. `["red cube", "bin"]`. |
| `subtasks` | no | Its steps in order, e.g. `["reach", "grasp", "lift", "place"]`. |

## Event kinds: `events.toml`

The kinds of [events](recording.md#events-kaptoevents) people and programs
may send, beside Kapto's own: what each is called, its colour on the
timeline, and whether it is usually a stretch, begun and ended, rather
than a moment, which is how the page offers it. Each kind is a table
under `kinds`, named by the kind: lowercase words joined by dots, not
beginning `kapto.` (Kapto's own) or `subtask.` (the tasks').

```toml
# events.toml
[kinds.grasp]
name = "Grasp"
color = "#4c9be8"
stretch = true
description = "The gripper closing on an object and holding it."

[kinds.slip]
name = "Slip"
color = "#e86a5a"
```

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | no | What people call it, e.g. `Grasp`; its kind if not given. |
| `color` | no | Its colour on the timeline, as `#rrggbb`. |
| `stretch` | no | Whether it is usually a stretch, begun and ended, rather than a moment: how the page offers it. `false` if not given. |
| `description` | no | A sentence about when to send it. |

Without the file, `note`, `problem`, `intervention` (a stretch) may be sent. Each task's subtasks are kinds
too, whatever the file says: `subtask.` then the subtask in
lowercase, anything but letters and digits as underscores (`Pick up`
is `subtask.pick_up`), each a stretch. A file with a problem is
reported, and the kinds there are without it are used meanwhile.
